title: Planning meals to save money
description: A loose weekly meal plan cuts the shopping bill, the waste, and the 6pm panic.

body.heading: Plan loosely, not rigidly
paragraphs: A meal plan does not need to be a strict timetable. List four or five dinners for the week, shop for those, and let the order flex with your energy and appetite. Loose plans survive real life; rigid ones get abandoned.
Build the plan around overlapping ingredients — the vegetables, grains, and proteins that appear in several meals — so nothing is bought for a single use and forgotten.

body.heading: One shop, fewer top-ups
paragraphs: Midweek top-up shops are where budgets leak: you go in for milk and leave with snacks, offers, and extras. A good list from a loose plan makes one main shop realistic.
Keep a running note of things as they run out. Writing it down in the moment beats reconstructing it in the shop aisle.

body.heading: Batch and freeze
paragraphs: Cooking double and freezing half turns one effort into two meals, and future busy-you gets a homemade ready meal for almost no extra cost.

takeaway: Plan four or five flexible dinners around shared ingredients, shop once, and freeze the extras.
